summary: Small pop-up notifications in the bottom-right corner, used for confirmations, errors and live incident alerts. Toasts stack up to four at a time, dismiss themselves after a timeout, pause while hovered and can run an action when clicked; their left edge shows the risk-level colour. main.js, the palette, the pages and the detail drawers all call `toast()`.

notes.text: File header: toasts are short notifications stacked in the bottom-right corner, with the risk-level colour as a stripe on their left edge.
Imports `$` (a `querySelector` shortcut) and the auto-escaping `html` template from dom.js.
Imports the motion-aware `animate` and the `spring` easing helper.
`MAX` caps how many toasts can be on screen at once, so a burst of live alerts can't fill the screen.

`toast()` takes one options object: a `title`, an optional `body`, an optional risk `level`, a `timeout` before it dismisses itself (default 5.2 seconds) and an optional `onClick` action. The `= {}` default makes calling it with no argument safe.
`#toasts` is the container in index.html. It has `aria-live="polite"`, so screen readers announce new toasts without interrupting the user.
Creates the toast element. A `lvl-${level}` class is added only when a level is given; CSS paints the left stripe in that level's colour and falls back to the accent colour otherwise.
`role="status"` marks the toast as an advisory status message for assistive technology.
Fills the toast with the escaped title and, if given, the escaped body. `String(...)` turns the `SafeHTML` object into the plain string `innerHTML` expects.
Adds the toast to the end of the container, so the newest one appears at the bottom of the stack.
The stacking limit: while there are more than four toasts, the oldest (the first child) is removed at once.
Entrance animation: the toast slides in from 40px to the right, fades in and grows from 97% to full size, with a slightly bouncy spring ease.
`timer` holds the id of the auto-dismiss timeout. It is declared here so the handlers below can cancel or restart it.
`dismiss()` first cancels any pending timer, so the toast can't be dismissed twice.
Waits for the exit animation (slide 30px right and fade out over 200ms), then removes the element from the page.
Closes `dismiss()`.
Clicking a toast runs its optional action (for example, opening the incident it announced) and then dismisses it.
Hover-pause: while the pointer is over the toast its countdown is cancelled, so it stays up for as long as someone is reading it.
When the pointer leaves, a new, shorter two-second countdown starts.
Starts the initial auto-dismiss countdown and closes the function.
